24.verdict: ahead of the channel's earlier Shorts at this age: 1054 views against a median of 732 (1.4x)

worked: The paradoxical statement hook ('The first pictures of the Moon's far side used American spy film') drove strong initial velocity, reaching 1,054 views and 42.9 views per hour at 24.6 hours, well above the channel average.
The historical reveal maintained audience approval, achieving a solid 4.3 likes per 100 views compared to the lower rates (2.4 to 3.9) on most previous ~1k-view videos.
hurt: Comment engagement was completely flat at 0 comments across 1,054 views, largely caused by a closed-loop summary ending ('That is how American spy film captured...') that offers no unresolved tension or prompt for viewers to respond.
diagnosis.change_next: Keep the bold paradox hook format, but replace the repetitive summary ending beat with an open-ended provocative question (e.g., asking whether using an adversary's tech was genius or desperation) to convert high view velocity into comment engagement.

72.verdict: level with the channel's earlier Shorts at this age: 1058 views against a median of 955 (1.1x)

worked: High algorithmic distribution and viewer approval: feed share reached 0.973 (97.3% of views from the Shorts feed) and likes per 100 hit 4.3, proving the premise effectively generated initial curiosity.
Strong early hold: watching at 5% reached 1.196, showing viewers did not immediately swipe in the first second or two thanks to the provocative opening claim.
hurt: Mid-script pacing drop: watching at 50% dropped steeply to 0.458 (and avg_viewed fell to 53.44%, noticeably below channel peers that held 0.55 to 0.59 at midpoint), caused by middle exposition detours about tidal locking and launch dates before delivering the spy film receipt.

Weak end retention: watching at the end slipped to 0.274, dragged down by an explicit summary sign-off in the final beat ('That is how American spy film captured...') that gave viewers an early signal to swipe away.
diagnosis.change_next: Move the core revelation (the downed US spy balloons) immediately after the hook beat and cut the explanatory detour about tidal locking, going straight from the spy balloon theft to the automated darkroom.
